title: Design System: Emule
scope: Website only: docs/index.html (GitHub Pages, pt-BR). The desktop app UI in src/renderer is a separate, older system and is out of scope.

display.purpose: The single hero headline on the caption plate. Uppercase, balanced wrap.

headline.purpose: Section titles, uppercase, max 18ch. Closing call uses clamp(2.4rem,6vw,4.4rem)/0.92; one-frame ruler clamp(1.9rem,3.6vw,2.8rem)/0.95.

title.purpose: Frame names, how-to step titles, active-frame caption, sub-heads, wordmark. Uppercase, 800, 1.3-1.7rem.

body.purpose: Running text in Archivo. Ledes 56ch, captions 60ch, notes and FAQ 70ch. Emphasis is 600 in Overexposed White.

label.purpose: Burn-ins, ruler captions, requirement labels, keycap legends. Uppercase, tabular numerals.

measurement.purpose: Measured values in the measurement log, always Time Yellow.

motion.name: frame-cut
motion.purpose: Caption change when a frame is selected; a cut, not a fade. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

motion.name: frame-develop
motion.purpose: Frame diagram switching between greyscale 42% and full colour. Only under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

focus.purpose: Global :focus-visible ring. The only non-measurement use of Time Yellow (with text selection and the skip link).

narrative.overview:
The site is a slow-motion latency test filmed frame by frame. Surfaces are footage-grey film stock separated by hard 1px rules; information is burned into the frames the way a high-speed camera overlays timecode, in an uppercase monospaced video-overlay face. One input travels mouse, USB, phone, decode, PC screen across a strip of five frames, and a yellow playhead walks a ruler underneath it. The page has no imagery beyond line-drawn diagrams; the phone's pixels are an overexposed off-white.

Colour is rationed by role, not by decoration. Everything is greyscale except two signals: yellow means time and measurement, green means input. Because each colour carries one meaning, a reader can tell at a glance that a yellow number was measured and that a green thing is something they (or their mouse) do. The voice is direct and technical: real ms, fps and Hz, nothing unmeasured.

Motion is a cut, not a tween. Frames change state in hard steps like scrubbing footage, and under reduced motion they change instantly.
keyCharacteristics: Footage-grey film stock on a near-black ground; depth by tone, never by shadow.
Burned-in OSD text (frame number, stage, measured value) on frames and steps.
Yellow is time and measurement; green is the input event and the download action.
Square geometry with 1px rules, corner crop marks on the selected frame.
Condensed uppercase display headlines over a neutral grotesque body.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: Yellow means time or a measured value; green means input or the download action. Nothing else gets colour. A number in yellow must be a real measurement; a decorative highlight in either colour breaks the code. Keyboard focus is the single sanctioned exception for yellow.

rules.name: The Green Is the Action Rule
rules.body: The only filled button on the site is the green download. Secondary actions are plain underlined links in white.

rules.name: The Burned-In Rule
rules.body: Burn-ins carry frame data (position like "QD 01/05" or "Passo 1/4", the stage, a measured value) and are set in the mono label style. They never restate or introduce the heading below them.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: Share Tech Mono is reserved for what the camera or the app would print: labels, keys, numbers. Prose is never set in it.

rules.name: The Tone-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface rises by moving one step lighter in the grey ramp, never by casting a shadow. The keycap's 3px bottom border is the only bevel, and it belongs to the keycap alone.

dos: **Do** reserve Time Yellow for measured values, rulers, the playhead and keyboard focus.
**Do** reserve Input Green for input events (click, touch point, mouse updates) and the download action.
**Do** separate everything with 1px Rule lines and step surfaces by grey tone (Film, Frame Stock, Raised Stock).
**Do** set burn-ins, labels, keys and numbers in Share Tech Mono, uppercase, tabular numerals.
**Do** move between states with hard cuts (`steps(2)`, 0.1–0.14s) and drop them under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** label illustrated frames as illustration and keep every number a real measurement.
donts: **Don't** use colour gradients, glows or drop shadows; the world is flat footage (solid single-colour `linear-gradient` fills that draw the crop marks are a drawing technique, not a gradient).
**Don't** colour anything yellow or green for decoration or emphasis.
**Don't** build cards with icon tiles or a floating phone mockup; content lives in frames and ruled rows.
**Don't** round corners beyond the button (2px) and keycap (4px).
**Don't** tween state changes with easing curves; cut between frames.
**Don't** apply this system to the desktop app's UI in `src/renderer`, which has its own older look.
